VULVAL SKIN HEALTH

Vulval lichen sclerosus care

A guide to diagnosis, prescribed treatment and ongoing review.

AT A GLANCE

What this care addresses

Lichen sclerosus can cause itchy white patches and fragile genital skin. It is not contagious or caused by poor hygiene. Scarring may cause tightness and discomfort. Skin changes need examination to establish their cause.

Patient information · Canada · Sources checked 8 September 2026

What this care addresses

Lichen sclerosus can cause itchy white patches and fragile genital skin. It is not contagious or caused by poor hygiene. Scarring may cause tightness and discomfort. Skin changes need examination to establish their cause.

NHS · Lichen sclerosus ↗

Assessment and care options

Prescription steroid ointment is commonly used to control symptoms. There is no cure, so follow-up and an individual maintenance plan matter. A clinician can explain medication use and whether specialist assessment is needed.

When to arrange care

Arrange review for a new lump, thickened area or an ulcer that does not heal. Lichen sclerosus carries a small increased risk of vulval cancer; ask how to monitor changes.

NHS · Lichen sclerosus ↗

Questions for your appointment

  • How certain is the diagnosis?
  • How should I use and review my prescription?
  • Which skin changes should prompt an appointment?

Planning a conversation in Canada

Ask your clinician where an assessment can be arranged and whether a referral is required. Confirm service availability, fees and any coverage directly with the provider and your insurer or provincial plan.
